To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effective interaction of global virtual teams over time is characterized by a series of incidents that are configured by aspects of their structural and process elements, and that effective global virtual teams have a deep rhythm of interaction that includes a series of incidents with varying levels of intensity and duration.

effective global virtual teams interact by configuring communication incidents to match the team's form, process, and decision complexity, and that these teams sequence these communication incidents into a deep rhythm of face-to-face and less intensive, shorter interactions using various media.
effective global virtual teams are able to create a deep rhythm of interaction incidents that fit the team's decision-making process and complexity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of global virtual teams, and the conditions that affect their effectiveness.
understanding global virtual team dynamics.
the processes that underlie global virtual team effectiveness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dynamics of global virtual teams are a function of the interaction between the structural elements of the group and the communication process elements, which in turn is a function of the complexity of the task.

the dynamics and effectiveness of global virtual teams are shaped by a series of interaction incidents that are sequenced in a rhythm of regular, face-to-face meetings interspersed with other, more intermittent interactions.
the global virtual team is not a team at all.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the global virtual team process is a series of communication episodes that are sequenced over time to create a deep rhythm of face-to-face interaction that is interspersed with other media.
effective global virtual teams are those that have a deep rhythm of communication incidents, and that these incidents are configured by aspects of team structure and process.
effective global virtual teams have a deep rhythm of interaction that is characterized by a sequence of incidents that fit the form and complexity of the decision process and the media used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
global virtual team dynamics are not static, but rather are dynamic and change over time.
global virtual teams can and do perform effectively over time, and that they can be managed to do so.
global virtual teams are more than the sum of their parts, and their performance is not simply a function of the quality of their individual interactions.
